memory_notes.title: Luke reads risk first, status second
memory_notes.content: Across 11 morning briefs the only sections Luke consistently opens within 30s are "Risks" and "Decisions needed". Status updates get skipped. Always order: risks → decisions → followups → cash → calendar.

memory_notes.title: Procurement approvals cluster late afternoon
memory_notes.content: Luke approves 80% of POs between 15:00 and 17:30 ET. Morning prompts to approve are ignored; afternoon batch reminders convert at ~90%.

memory_notes.title: Acme Steel >72h silence = escalate
memory_notes.content: Pattern from last 6 escalations: if Jorge Ramirez (Acme) goes >72h without written reply, Luke either calls personally or asks David to escalate to Acme VP. Auto-flag at 72h.

memory_notes.title: Henry Whitcomb wants margin walk on slide 1
memory_notes.content: Board chair has asked for margin walk as opening slide in 4 of last 5 board packages. Confirmed verbally at March board meeting. Default to this layout.

memory_notes.title: Karen Liu's variance narratives are always clean
memory_notes.content: Toledo controller produces tightest variance commentary of the four plants. Sarah trusts her numbers. Use Toledo commentary as reference quality for plant comparisons.

memory_notes.title: Deloitte PBC items — start 4 weeks out
memory_notes.content: Q1 audit committee post-mortem: 3 weeks of PBC prep was too tight. Renee Fischer notices when items go amber. Default to 4 week lead time on PBC list.

memory_notes.title: Slack DMs from Sarah = urgent, email = standard
memory_notes.content: Sarah Chen only DMs in Slack when she needs same-day action. Email is for non-urgent. Surface Slack DMs from Sarah in real-time, route emails to standard inbox flow.

memory_notes.title: Tuesday 9am treasury sync — non-negotiable
memory_notes.content: Standing weekly with Priya Nair. Luke only skips when board prep collides; otherwise this is the most consistent meeting on his calendar.

memory_notes.title: Hard cap 350 words on AM brief
memory_notes.content: Luke complained twice in March about brief length. Anything over 350 words gets skimmed. Use "expand" toggle for detail.

memory_notes.title: Board meeting cadence: 3rd Wednesday monthly
memory_notes.content: Standing board meeting 3rd Wednesday of each month. Pre-read due 48h ahead = EOD Monday.

memory_notes.title: Filter benefits/HR/all-hands from briefing
memory_notes.content: Luke confirmed: do not include HR, recruiting, benefits enrollment, or all-hands announcements in AM brief. Route to "personal" category and snooze.

memory_notes.title: Marcus Reyes is the partner for variance context
memory_notes.content: Before any variance memo or board narrative, Luke checks with Marcus for operational color. Marcus prefers Teams over Slack. Loop him in early.

memory_notes.title: Ft Worth standing topic in board narrative
memory_notes.content: Capex overrun on Line 3 has been mentioned in every board package since March. Will continue through commissioning (est. Q3). Pre-populate slide.

memory_notes.title: Group follow-ups by category, not by date
memory_notes.content: Luke explicitly asked: never show flat list. Always group by procurement / treasury / audit / vendor / board / operations.

memory_notes.title: Reminders > dashboards for Luke
memory_notes.content: When given a choice of "passive dashboard widget" vs "active reminder", Luke acts on reminders 3-4x more often. Default to proactive push.

memory_notes.title: Approval lead time KPI tracked on dashboard
memory_notes.content: Luke watches procurement approval lead time daily. Target 7d, current 14d. Surface this metric in AM brief whenever it moves >1d.

memory_notes.title: Revolver covenant: 3.5x leverage, currently 2.8x
memory_notes.content: Maintenance covenant on revolver is 3.5x net debt/EBITDA. Trailing 12-month leverage currently 2.8x, trend up. Surface when crossing 3.0x.

memory_notes.title: Luke prefers prep packet 60 min before external meetings
memory_notes.content: 60 minutes before any meeting with Deloitte, PNC, board members, or vendors, Luke wants a packet. Internal meetings: no packet needed.
